title: Launch cascade scrapbook — warmup cohort choreography
content:
Context:
- Preparing progressive rollout for runtime v2.8.0 (primarily attention-kernel improvements + KV cache fixes). Goal: expose hosted API traffic to v2.8 with minimal user-facing regressions, keep token/unit-cost within 5% of baseline, and ensure fast fallback to v1.9 shard if needed.

High-level plan (narrative):
1) Preflight: bake images on staging, run canary harness with synthetic customer traffic for 24h, run end-to-end smoke suite.
2) Warmup cohorts: introduce micro-cohorts (orbit1 -> orbit2 -> orbit3) that exercise high QPS short-input and low QPS long-context paths separately.
3) Canary: slow ramp with telemetry gates; after each jump, verify SLA signals for 30 minutes before next increment.
4) Global roll: if all cohorts stable, move to percentage-based ramp to 100% over 6h with rollback checkpoints.

Cohort definitions (naming + rationale):
- orbit-1: 0.5% of traffic, internal + opt-in beta customers. Purpose: sanity check routing, auth, tokenization changes. Duration: 1h baseline, then 3h synthetic soak.
- orbit-2: 2% traffic, PLG users (web + mobile) low-context requests (<256 tokens). Purpose: throughput and latency regression detection. Duration: 2h.
- orbit-3: 5% traffic, mixed long and short requests, includes paid customers (small set). Purpose: model kernel and KV cache warm behavior. Duration: 4h.

Safety thresholds (hard thresholds to trigger immediate rollback):
- error rate (5xx) > 0.8% for 5 minutes -> rollback.
- p95 latency increase > 200ms vs baseline for 10 minutes -> pause and investigate.
- token cost per 1k tokens increase > 7% sustained for 30 minutes -> halt.
- client-side feedback: any customer-reported hallucination/regression rate from CS channel flagged -> rollback candidate.

Telemetry to watch (dashboard tiles / key traces):
- API success rate (2xx vs 5xx), per-route, per-region.
- Token throughput and unit-cost estimator (tokens/sec, tokens/response).
- p50/p95/p99 latency by service lane (short/long).
- KV cache hit ratio by model-shard.
- GPU utilization and queue depth per host.
- TLS handshake errors and connection churn.
- Top 10 slowest trace samples (trace ids pinned to incident channel).

Preflight checklist (quick):
- [ ] Staging deployments green (smoke test pass)
- [ ] Model artifact signature verified and pinned in artifact catalog
- [ ] Canary config prepared (routes, weights, rollout windows)
- [ ] Pager rotations and on-call list notified (channel #releases + explicit pings)
- [ ] Warmup synthetic traffic script ready (path: infra/playbooks/warmup-v2.8.js)
- [ ] Backfill plan for KV caches documented
- [ ] PRs merged + runtime binary baked: runtime:v2.8.0-20251102

Roll & rollback commands (notes to self):
- To pin route to v2.8 for a subset: redwoodctl route update --name hosted-text --weight v2.8=0.005 --cohort orbit-1
- To divert region: redwoodctl routing set --region eu-west-1 --variant v1.9 --force (escape hatch)
- Quick rollback to v1.9 global: redwoodctl route update --name hosted-text --weight v1.9=1.0 && redwoodctl rollout abort --release v2.8
- To scale up warmers: k run -i --rm warmup-generator --image=registry/warmup:v1 -- /bin/warmup --qps=50 --profile=short

Observability runbook (first 15m after jump):
- T+0: verify deployment reached targets on infra (hosts up, containers healthy).
- T+5: check success rate and p95 for the cohort. If either breached threshold, initiate pause/rollback.
- T+15: sample traces for any slow tail, check KV cache heatmap for cold shards.
- T+30: confirm cost metrics stable and no auto-scaler thrash.

Open questions / unknowns (to resolve before next run):
- How will client SDK timeouts interact with longer-tail model calls under new kernel micro-batching? Need to run longer synthetic sessions.
- Does v2.8 change streaming chunk sizes in a way that affects function-calling integrations? QA to verify.
- Can we produce automated alerts that correlate latency spikes with KV cache miss buckets? (File ticket if not available).

Post-rollout checklist (notes):
- Export cohort telemetry and attach to ENG-1427.
- Run model-quality quick eval on sample prompt set (promptset: rollout-smoke-2025-11).
- Contact customer-success for any beta feedback within 24h, escalate critical regressions.
- Prepare tight follow-up: throttling knobs if token-cost creeps above plan.

Personal quick heuristics (tacit):
- If p95 regression is localized to one region, prefer region-level diversion over global rollback.
- Small increases in p50 are tolerable if p99 and error rates are stable.
- Always keep a ready image/tag for v1.9 and a documented fast-path command for global revert.

Notes-to-self / fragments: 
- When warming KV cache, prime with high-frequency prefixes from historical sample. Avoid priming full long-context dataset (expensive).
- Remember to disable synthetic warmers after cohort stabilization (they hide real user signals).
- Slack pings: @oncall-releases, @eng-core, @cs-bugtriage.

Appendix: workloads to run in staging (short commands)
- run smoke: ./tools/smoke.sh --env staging --suite basic --duration 30m
- synth ramp: node infra/playbooks/warmup-v2.8.js --cohort orbit-1 --qps 5 --duration 3h
- trace gather: redwoodctl traces query --since 1h --filter p95>200 --out traces/t1.json

End notes: this is a personal notebook — rough, keep iterating. Next pass: formalize into a release doc for the team, include exact runbook with escalation contacts and make sure alerting plays are in place.
